RQ1.question: Why do users repeatedly buy from the same categories?

categories.name: Speed on daily essentials builds routine
categories.description: Reviews praising 8-10 minute delivery for everyday groceries, food, and 'daily needs' items (e.g. as_14221102265, gp_6066c3e3, gp_c8836b7d, gp_327d4a5f) describe fast delivery turning routine restocking into a habit.

categories.name: Dairy repeatedly arrives spoiled but is reordered anyway
categories.description: Reviews describing milk, curd/buttermilk, and paneer curdling or spoiling on multiple separate occasions, often from self-described regular/loyal customers still ordering that category (gp_3e097984, gp_1f6f10dd, gp_79357c9c, gp_cbddfa4f, gp_3da86bc9, as_14228692257, gp_21c76a02).

categories.name: Produce quality is a recurring gamble
categories.description: Reviews about fruits and vegetables arriving rotten, unripe, torn, or bitten across repeated orders, showing users keep buying this category despite consistent disappointment (as_14309161557, gp_faa0a551, as_14298500733, gp_583275f2, as_14297225931).

categories.name: Casual habitual language in Hindi/Hinglish
categories.description: Short, affectionate, habit-toned comments (roz mangata hun, sabse sasta, mera kaam asaan ho jaata hai) that frame repeat ordering as an unreflective daily habit rather than a reasoned choice (yt_UgzdftOmzQLLhI910CF4AaABAg, gp_1b4a0430, gp_98f72de0, gp_3abfe7f0, yt_UgwmCeiIYm5xIkQXw2Z4AaABAg).

categories.name: Go-to for emergencies and last-minute needs
categories.description: Reviews framing the app as their fallback for urgent, occasional needs rather than full grocery shopping — 'emergency purchase', 'last minute needs', 'urgency' (gp_b0eb607e, gp_92fcafaf, gp_15fe56f7, gp_3897874f, as_14307506016).

categories.name: Years-long loyalty cited right before switching apps
categories.description: Reviews that establish long tenure ('regular customer since years', '2 years', '5 months') as evidence of habitual repeat buying, then describe the specific repeated failure that finally pushed them toward Blinkit/Instamart or uninstalling (as_14306958436, as_14313342610, as_14233386056, as_14281697253, as_14282329900, as_14311630110).

categories.name: Cheaper than Blinkit/Instamart keeps orders coming
categories.description: Reviews that explicitly compare price to competitors (Blinkit, Instamart, market rate) and cite lower prices/cashback/free-cash offers as the reason they keep ordering the same staples (gp_d9b5833a, yt_UgwnZFk18X817UjPzHh4AaABAg, gp_3a828736, yt_UgyAk-llsgDDpNpRh_p4AaABAg).

categories.name: Rising fees erode the habit of small frequent orders
categories.description: Reviews tying repeat ordering directly to low/no delivery and handling charges, and noting that fee hikes (handling charge, raised minimum order) cut their order frequency (gp_190d9ebf, gp_9cfecc20, as_14276434786, gp_ebacda12).

categories.name: Frozen items melt every time
categories.description: Reviews specifically calling out ice cream and frozen snacks arriving melted or with broken seals on repeated orders, a narrow but recurring product-category complaint (gp_042a7fa5, as_14291315241, as_14309615442).

RQ2.question: What prevents exploration of new categories?

categories.name: Refund and complaint denials discourage retrying orders
categories.description: Reviews where customer support refuses refunds/replacements despite photo evidence, sends templated or bot responses, or blames the customer, leaving users feeling any future order (in a new category) carries unrecoverable risk.

categories.name: Spoiled perishables kill trust in fresh items
categories.description: Reviews reporting spoiled milk, rotten vegetables/fruits, expired paneer/yogurt/juices, or stale produce delivered repeatedly, leading users to say they've stopped or will stop ordering fresh/perishable categories altogether.

categories.name: Delivery delays and partner misconduct overshadow product choice
categories.description: Reviews about late deliveries, rude or dishonest delivery partners, tip extortion, or failed handoffs, where frustration with the delivery experience itself (not product selection) dominates and discourages broader app usage.

categories.name: Fraud and scam perception blocks any further engagement
categories.description: Reviews explicitly labeling Zepto a 'fraud', 'scam', 'chor app', or 'loot', often citing manipulated order history or deceptive practices, reflecting a general distrust that suppresses exploring anything beyond routine repeat purchases.

categories.name: Rising prices and hidden fees make experimentation feel costly
categories.description: Reviews about handling charges, delivery fee hikes, surge pricing, or price increases on familiar items, which make customers reluctant to spend on unfamiliar or non-essential categories they might not need.

categories.name: Wrong or substituted items erode confidence to try new products
categories.description: Reviews describing receiving a different item/brand/flavor than ordered (e.g. wrong noodles, wrong ice cream flavor, wrong t-shirt promo, out-of-stock swaps), which makes customers wary of ordering unfamiliar items they can't verify in advance.

categories.name: Missing or short-quantity deliveries reduce willingness to add items
categories.description: Reviews reporting missing items, partial quantities (e.g. half the ordered weight), or items silently dropped from an order, making customers cautious about adding new or additional items to a cart.

categories.name: Defective non-grocery items sour trust in general merchandise
categories.description: Reviews about faulty electronics (kettle), damaged mugs, used/opened products, or apparel return issues, where bad experiences with non-food categories specifically make customers hesitant to buy anything outside daily grocery staples.

categories.name: Melted frozen goods deter reordering ice cream
categories.description: Reviews specifically about ice cream or frozen items arriving melted or liquid, with support denying refunds by claiming the product was fine at dispatch, discouraging any further ordering of frozen categories.

RQ3.question: How are new products discovered today?

categories.name: Word-of-mouth and social recommendation to download
categories.description: Reviews explicitly telling others to download or avoid the app ('sabhi log download karo', 'maine sabko bola na use kare'), showing peer recommendation as a discovery channel for the platform and its catalog.

categories.name: Dissatisfaction pushes users to explore competitor apps
categories.description: Reviews naming Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, JioMart or BigBasket as where they'll go instead after a bad Zepto experience — competitor products get discovered as a byproduct of switching apps.

categories.name: Deep-discount bundles trigger impulse purchases
categories.description: Reviews mentioning ultra-cheap or bundled items (₹1 store, ₹10-for-10 Lays packets, buy-1-get-3, dove soap + free t-shirt combos) that pull users into buying products they weren't originally looking for.

categories.name: In-app banners and saver sections spotlight products
categories.description: Reviews referencing specific in-app placements like the 'stock up' banner, 'super saver' section, or Zepto Cafe promos that surface products the user wouldn't have searched for directly.

categories.name: Referral codes as an unused discovery channel
categories.description: The single review noting inability to see or share a referral code, pointing to referral-based discovery as a mechanism present but broken/underused.

categories.name: Community and local-vendor framing shapes what's bought
categories.description: Reviews invoking regional or community identity (Marwari community in Mumbai, 'vocal for local', support for offline shopkeepers) that frame purchases in terms of community relevance rather than app-driven discovery.

categories.name: Cross-app price comparison surfaces items
categories.description: Reviews where users mention comparing the same product's price across Zepto, JioMart, Blinkit or BigBasket (e.g. dosa batter, choco roll, vegetables) — discovery happens by checking multiple apps side-by-side rather than browsing one.

categories.name: Wallet cash and coupon balance dictates what gets ordered
categories.description: Reviews describing choosing items specifically to spend free cash, zepto cash, or coupon credit (e.g. buying a bread + Kurkure to hit a minimum), showing discovery driven by available promo balance rather than need.

RQ4.question: What role do habits play in purchase behavior?

categories.name: App as default first choice, unprompted loyalty
categories.description: Reviews where users describe automatically defaulting to this app over alternatives out of ingrained habit — 'I always prefer Zepto first', 'Always zepto', multi-year regular customers who order 'everyday' or for '5 months'/'2 years' without needing a specific reason.

categories.name: Habitual reliance on daily staples
categories.description: Reviews describing the app as woven into everyday routines for milk, vegetables, groceries and other essentials, framing it as a default part of daily life rather than an occasional purchase (e.g. 'daily basis', 'dairy and vegetables buying', 'good app for daily needs', 'daily uses').

categories.name: Speed conditions users into instant-gratification ordering
categories.description: Reviews crediting minute-level delivery speed for making the app habit-forming ('order at anytime and get anything in minutes', '8 min', 'jaldi aata hai'), including explicit self-aware framing of the app breeding laziness/complacency ('making life easier and lazier', 'making customers lazy and relax').

categories.name: Late-night ordering routine collides with capacity limits
categories.description: Reviews specifically about habitual late-night or high-demand-hour ordering being undermined by cancellations or disabled instant delivery, frustrating a routine the user had built around the app's availability.

categories.name: Trust-breaking incidents override years of habitual use
categories.description: Reviews from self-identified long-time or high-spend regulars (₹10,000/month, 2 years, 'used everyday') who describe a single severe failure — melted/rotten goods, refund stonewalling, defective product, repeated wrong items — as the trigger that broke the habit entirely, leading to uninstalling or swearing off the app.

categories.name: Habit reinforced by convenience perks and recognition
categories.description: Reviews where cashback, discounts, or wanting recognition as a repeat customer (referral option, coupons for 'regular customers') are cited as what keeps the habitual ordering going, including complaints when loyalty isn't rewarded despite frequent use.

categories.name: Minimum-order/fee changes shrink order frequency
categories.description: Reviews where a policy change (raising minimum order value from 99 to 149, added delivery-partner surcharges) is described as directly reducing how often the user now orders, showing habit is sensitive to friction at the transaction level.

categories.name: Reliability gaps push habitual users to rival apps
categories.description: Reviews describing habit persisting toward the category (quick-commerce ordering) but shifting away from this specific app when it underdelivers, explicitly naming a switch to Instamart or other apps as the new default when this app's instant delivery or fulfillment fails.

categories.name: Perceived societal shift from shopping trips to app habit
categories.description: The single meta-level review framing quick-commerce apps as changing broader consumer behavior — replacing the habit of physically going out for grocery shopping with app-based ordering across the population, not just personal use.

RQ5.question: What information is missing before users try a new category?

categories.name: Dispute resolution process and evidence requirements opaque
categories.description: Reviews describing being asked for photos/videos and then still denied refunds via template responses, showing users don't know in advance what proof is required or how disputes will actually be handled if something goes wrong.

categories.name: Expiry-date reliability and tampering unknown
categories.description: Reviews reporting expired, near-expiry, or date-altered products (erased/reprinted expiry labels), showing users have no way to verify shelf-life accuracy before purchase.

categories.name: Packaging and hygiene handling standards unclear
categories.description: Reviews noting products delivered without carry bags, handed over loose/hand-to-hand, or with damaged/torn packaging, indicating users don't know what physical condition to expect on arrival.

categories.name: No-return policy for perishables undisclosed
categories.description: Reviews where users learn only after ordering that opened food packets (paneer, milk, jaggery, vegetables) cannot be returned even when spoiled, and note there's no way to check freshness without opening the seal first.

categories.name: Warehouse and sourcing quality controls invisible
categories.description: Reviews alleging dirty dark stores, fungus on products, or unverified freshness at the sourcing stage, suggesting users have no visibility into how or where items are stored before dispatch.

categories.name: Frozen item melting risk not signaled upfront
categories.description: Numerous reviews about ice cream, frozen desserts, and cold drinks arriving melted or warm because there's no visible cold-chain guarantee or insulated packaging commitment before ordering temperature-sensitive items.

categories.name: Silent substitution of ordered brand or product
categories.description: Reviews where a different product, brand, or pack size was delivered without prior notice or consent (e.g., Amul Moti instead of Amul Red Tetra milk), leaving users unaware substitutions are possible.

categories.name: Quantity or weight shortfall goes undetected until delivery
categories.description: Reviews describing receiving less quantity/weight than ordered (e.g., half the onion weight, missing items from multi-item orders) with no pre-purchase indication this could happen.

RQ6.question: Which user segments are more experimental?

categories.name: Passive offer-seekers, not experimenters
categories.description: Generic positive or neutral reviews about liking discounts, cashback, or low platform fees with no comparison, testing, or trial behavior described — a baseline non-experimental segment for contrast.

categories.name: Cross-app extenders of the experiment
categories.description: Commenters who want the same mass-order test repeated on Swiggy, Zomato, Rapido, Amazon, or with taxis/flights, showing a segment eager to generalize one experiment across many services rather than just Zepto.

categories.name: Viral mass-order test replicators
categories.description: YouTube commenters proposing or having done the '40+ people order the same item from one restaurant/store at the same time' stunt on Zepto, mostly young social-media-driven users curious about backend/delivery behavior under load.

categories.name: Multi-account and edge-case testers
categories.description: Users suggesting more elaborate variants: ordering from 10 accounts, cancelling 3 minutes after ordering, or delivering to someone else's location — pushing the experiment into stress-testing territory.

categories.name: Cross-platform price comparers
categories.description: App store reviewers who actively benchmark Zepto's prices item-by-item against DMart, Flipkart, Amazon, and JioMart (e.g. 'Waffy 80rs on Flipkart', 'DMart mein 90 ka mil jaega'), showing deal-hunting behavior rather than brand loyalty.

categories.name: Coupon and free-cash mechanic testers
categories.description: Users who deliberately probe minimum-order rules, discount coupons, or free-cash offers to see if they apply (e.g. ordering just below the ₹99 minimum with free cash), then report whether the mechanic worked or failed.

categories.name: Burned first-timers who won't retry
categories.description: One-star reviewers describing a single experimental first order that failed (wrong/bad product, blocked coupon, no support resolution), framing the app as untrustworthy after just one trial rather than repeat experimentation.

categories.name: First-time switchers from established apps
categories.description: Reviewers describing their first Zepto order after being an Amazon/Flipkart user, explicitly testing delivery speed or product quality as a trial before deciding to migrate.

categories.name: Spoiled, expired, or damaged goods not made right
categories.description: Reviews reporting rotten vegetables, expired milk/curd/dates, melted ice cream, or torn/used packaging, where the resolution offered is denial or a template apology instead of replacement or refund.

categories.name: No path to a human beyond chatbot
categories.description: Reviews describing Zepto's support as an AI bot ('Zap') or scripted chat/email that loops, ends chats prematurely, or gives no phone number or human agent to escalate to.

categories.name: Zepto cash and payment features malfunction
categories.description: Reviews where Zepto cash/free cash is disabled, on hold, or not selectable at checkout, or where payment is deducted but shown as failed/cancelled with delayed refunds.

categories.name: Instant-delivery promise not honored
categories.description: Reviews where the quoted 6-10 minute delivery time balloons to 1-3 hours with no real-time update, or instant delivery silently switches to next-day slots.

categories.name: Wrong item sent with no correction mechanism
categories.description: Reviews describing receipt of an incorrect, substitute, or non-veg-for-veg item where the app offers no way to flag it for exchange rather than a fresh complaint loop.

categories.name: Refund or return marked failed despite pickup
categories.description: Reviews where a return was physically picked up by the delivery partner but the app shows 'return failed,' or a refund is promised/'completed' yet never credited to the account or Zepto cash wallet.

categories.name: Cannot cancel or edit an order after placing
categories.description: Reviews wanting a way to cancel accidental or delayed orders themselves, since the app provides no self-serve cancel option and bots sometimes cancel orders without consent instead.

categories.name: Delivery partner contact and last-mile coordination
categories.description: Reviews wanting a way to reach the delivery rider directly (phone number) or better address-matching support, citing riders unreachable by call or unable to locate the address.

categories.name: No warranty or bill support for electronics
categories.description: Reviews about electronics (bulbs, printers, mice) where Zepto won't issue a proper invoice/warranty card or redirects customers to the manufacturer instead of honoring after-sales support.

categories.name: No Hindi-language interface
categories.description: Reviews explicitly asking for a Hindi-language option in the app, since it currently offers none.
